source.citation: Chicago Public Library, "Technology That Changed Chicago: Gaslight", Chicago Public Library blog
what_it_does_not_supply: which streets were lit by gas and which by electricity in 1904, or Prairie Avenue's in particular
how many lamps, their hours, or who lit them
whether any Prairie Avenue house was lit by gas, by electricity or by both
what_it_supplies: THE CITY STILL LIT SOME STREETS BY GAS in the early 1900s: the city, which regulated Peoples Gas, 'still used gas streetlights in some areas'.

GAS MANTLES from the 1890s: 'Gas mantles, producing brighter light with only one-twelfth the gas consumption, became available in the 1890s', so a gas lamp of 1904 can burn a mantle's whiter light rather than an open flame's.
ELECTRIC LIGHT ARRIVING: 'Electric lights were common by 1909'.
